title: Controls playbook one-on-one prep (Amelia)
content:
Purpose: quick prep notes for my 1:1 with Samir (security engineer) and Jordan (audit lead). Focus: SOC2 control walkthrough, vendor assurance gaps, and an action list to show audit readiness for next quarter. This is a scratchpad — informal, lots of TODOs and questions.

Context / objective
- Demo progress on control remediations we promised in the Q4 remediation plan. Primary ask from audit: show evidence flow for user access reviews, vendor onboarding docs, and incident detection/triage timeline.
- Secondary: align on who will own the evidence collection script (Samir?), finish vendor attestation tracker (Jordan), and decide on next steps for ISO scoping (we may need to include a new GCP project).

Meeting goals
- Validate current evidence artifacts and identify missing items for SOC2 Subservice Org / Redwood-hosted API.
- Agree owners + deadlines for vendor risk items flagged as 'high' in SEC-842.
- Walk through playbook steps we will show auditors (access review, change control, backup verification, incident log sampling).

Quick summary of where we are
- Access reviews: last run 2025-09-15 (automated exports exist), but no signed manager attestations for two groups (Dedicated Ops, Private Deploy). Need manager approvals collected.
- Change control: PR -> staging -> prod gating exists, but our traceability report is missing approvals for Jan-Feb 2026. Dev leads blame CI rollup bug.
- Vendor risk: 14 vendors onboarded in past year; 3 now flagged 'high' (kms-provider-x, telemetry-analytics, model-hosting-partner). KMS provider has expired attestation (needs new SOC2/ISO report).
- Incident logs: PagerDuty to Splunk pipeline intact; only problem is log retention policy for infra-alerts is 90 days in Splunk but our policy requires 180 for SOC2 evidence.

Agenda (15min prep / 30min meeting)
- 0–5m: Quick status from Jordan (audit lead) — what auditors want in next evidence bundle
- 5–12m: Walk access review artifacts and signer gaps (Amelia + Samir)
- 12–22m: Vendor riskiest items — review attestation status and mitigation timeline (Jordan)
- 22–28m: Show checklist for change control traceability sample we can produce in 48 hours (Samir)
- 28–30m: Confirm owners and deadlines; quick sync cadence for next two weeks

Notes to self (things to surface)
- Bring one concrete example: User access CSV for Dedicated Ops group (exported 2025-11-20) that shows last login, role, and manager. If manager cell blank -> need to show target actions.
- Bring artifact: sample signed attestation email from Manager (format we want auditors to accept). We should propose a one-click approval workflow via Slack + Doc signature.
- Ask Jordan: will auditors accept a combined signing email + audit export, or do they need unique internal tool attestations?
- Samir: ask whether we can run an immediate re-attestation request via vendor-portal API for kms-provider-x. If not, what manual evidence will satisfy them?

Action items (owners + target dates)
- Amelia: compile evidence bundle outline and email to Jordan + Samir by EOD today (2026-03-10). Include list of missing artifacts and proposed substitutes. (HIGH)
- Samir: prototype an 'evidence collector' script to pull last 6 months of access review exports, change control approvals, and incident samples. ETA: 2026-03-15. (MED-HIGH)
- Jordan: contact auditors to confirm acceptance criteria for manager attestation (email vs tool) and vendor attestation cutoffs. ETA: 2026-03-12. (HIGH)
- Riley: update vendor tracker spreadsheet with current attestation expiry dates and a recommended remediation plan for kms-provider-x. ETA: 2026-03-14. (MED)
- Ops: extend Splunk infra-alert retention to 180 days for security-indexed logs — raise CF runbook change. ETA: 2026-03-18. (MED)

Evidence checklist (what auditors will likely request)
- Access review exports (CSV) for last two cycles + manager attestation emails
- User deprovisioning logs (API calls, ticket refs)
- Change control PR history for sample of 10 PRs across Jan–Mar 2026 with approvals and timestamps
- Vendor letters-of-attestation or SOC2/ISO reports for top-10 vendors by risk
- Backup verification report for production DB (last 6 restore tests) + runbook
- Incident response timelines for 3 sampled incidents: alert -> triage -> remediation -> postmortem

Potential substitutes / mitigations (if we can't get originals quickly)
- For missing manager signatures: propose an internal manager attestation form with email thread + screenshot of GSuite approval as temporary evidence
- For vendor attestations: combine contractual SOW, current security questionnaire, and latest penetration test summary if SOC2 report not available
- For change control gaps: produce a timestamped change rollup from CI plus retrospective sign-off from engineering manager

Risks / open questions (call them out early)
- If auditors insist on third-party SOC2 report for KMS provider, procurement timeline could be 6–8 weeks — we need a backup key-wrapping mitigation for customer data in the meantime.
- Data residency for Private customers — do we need an updated scope addendum for the new EU region? Ask legal if a simple amendment suffices.
- Evidence collection script telemetry: do we need to record who ran the collector to preserve chain-of-custody?

Follow-ups after meeting (planned)
- Quick 20-minute triage on 2026-03-11 to confirm scripts + sample outputs
- Weekly 1:1 touchpoint until 2026-04-01: Friday 10am standup with small working group (Amelia, Samir, Jordan, Riley)
- Deliver preliminary evidence bundle to auditors by 2026-03-20 (tentative)

Prep checklist for me (pre-meeting tasks)
- Attach sample CSV and manager email to calendar invite (done?)
- Draft brief email template for manager attestation (example text included below)
- Print short runbook for Splunk retention change and change-control CI bug notes

Manager attestation email template (quick)
"Hi <Manager>,

As part of our quarterly access review for Redwood systems, please confirm that the users listed in the attached CSV under your team are authorized to keep their current roles and access. Reply with 'I confirm' and date. If you disagree with any user, reply with the username and reason and we will open a deprovisioning ticket.

Thanks,
Amelia"

Quick brain-dump ideas (not for meeting unless asked)
- Add a lightweight one-click attestation flow via Slack + Google Form, store signed responses in encrypted Google Drive folder with audit metadata
- Consider short-lived access tokens for private deployments to reduce long-term permission noise
- Vendor continuous monitoring: set up Riskified/ORCA-like scanner for vendor external cert expiration alerts

End notes: keep small, keep focused. The auditors want repeatable, auditable artifacts more than perfection. Demonstrate remediation intent and ownership.
